# paperclip_agent (Resource)

Manages a Paperclip agent, an AI employee of a company.

Agents are created directly, without a hire approval. The API only allows that when the company has `require_board_approval_for_new_agents` set to `false`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "paperclip_agent" "producer" {
  company_id   = paperclip_company.studio.id
  name         = "Producer"
  role         = "ceo"
  title        = "Executive Producer"
  capabilities = "Owns budgets and schedules, and decides which films get made."

  adapter_type = "process"
  adapter_config = jsonencode({
    command    = "python3"
    args       = ["agents/producer.py"]
    cwd        = "/srv/greenlight"
    timeoutSec = 300
  })

  runtime_config = jsonencode({
    heartbeat = {
      enabled     = true
      intervalSec = 300
    }
  })

  budget_monthly_cents = 10000
}

# A whole team from one definition. Each member reports to the producer.
locals {
  crew = {
    director = { title = "Director", capabilities = "Turns scripts into shot lists and reviews dailies." }
    editor   = { title = "Editor", capabilities = "Assembles cuts and prepares deliverables." }
  }
}

resource "paperclip_agent" "crew" {
  for_each = local.crew

  company_id   = paperclip_company.studio.id
  name         = each.value.title
  title        = each.value.title
  capabilities = each.value.capabilities
  reports_to   = paperclip_agent.producer.id

  adapter_type = "http"
  adapter_config = jsonencode({
    url     = "https://agents.example.com/${each.key}/heartbeat"
    method  = "POST"
    headers = { Authorization = "Bearer ${var.agent_webhook_token}" }
  })

  metadata = jsonencode({
    persona = each.key
  })
}

variable "agent_webhook_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# An agent with its own instructions, a skill and no authority to hire.
resource "paperclip_agent" "writer" {
  company_id   = paperclip_company.studio.id
  name         = "Screenwriter"
  reports_to   = paperclip_agent.producer.id
  adapter_type = "codex_local"

  instructions      = file("${path.module}/agents/writer/AGENTS.md")
  skills            = [paperclip_skill.greenlight.key]
  can_create_agents = false
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `adapter_type` (String) Adapter that runs the agent, such as `process`, `http`, `codex_local` or `opencode_local`. See the Paperclip adapter documentation for the full list.
- `company_id` (String) Identifier of the company the agent works for. Changing this replaces the agent.
- `name` (String) Name of the agent.

### Optional

- `adapter_config` (String) Adapter-specific settings as a JSON object, usually written with `jsonencode()`. Only the keys you declare are tracked: defaults that Paperclip adds on its own are ignored, and values the API redacts are assumed to be unchanged. When the attribute is omitted, the value stored by Paperclip is kept as is.

~> Plain values under `env` are stored in the Terraform state. Prefer secret references for credentials.
- `budget_monthly_cents` (Number) Monthly spending limit for the agent, in cents. `0` (the default) means no limit.
- `can_create_agents` (Boolean) Whether the agent may hire other agents. Paperclip normally allows this by default, so set it to `false` to keep the organisation as declared.
- `can_create_skills` (Boolean) Whether the agent may add skills to the company library. Paperclip allows this by default.
- `capabilities` (String) Free-form description of what the agent is good at. Other agents use it to decide who gets a task.
- `instructions` (String) Content of the agent's instruction entry file, usually `AGENTS.md`, typically loaded with `file()`. Only adapters with managed instruction bundles support this, such as `codex_local` and `opencode_local`; `process` and `http` do not. When omitted, Paperclip's default instructions are left alone, and removing the attribute stops tracking the file without changing it. Agents can edit their own instructions, which shows up as drift. Other files in the bundle are not managed.
- `metadata` (String) Arbitrary metadata as a JSON object.
- `reports_to` (String) Identifier of the agent this agent reports to. Omit for the top of the organisation.
- `role` (String) Role of the agent in the organisation, such as `ceo`, `engineer`, `designer`, `pm`, `qa`, `researcher` or `general`. Defaults to `general`.
- `runtime_config` (String) Runtime settings as a JSON object, for example `jsonencode({ heartbeat = { enabled = true, intervalSec = 300 } })`. Only the keys you declare are tracked: defaults that Paperclip adds on its own are ignored, and values the API redacts are assumed to be unchanged. When the attribute is omitted, the value stored by Paperclip is kept as is.
- `skills` (Set of String) Complete set of skills assigned to the agent, as skill keys such as `paperclip_skill.example.key`. Skills assigned any other way are removed. An empty set removes all skills. When omitted, assignments are left alone, and removing the attribute stops tracking them without changing them.
- `title` (String) Job title shown in the organisation chart.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the agent.
- `status` (String) Current status of the agent, such as `idle`, `running`, `paused` or `error`.
- `url_key` (String) URL-safe key of the agent, derived from its name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Agents are imported by their identifier.
terraform import paperclip_agent.producer 8b1f6a0c-2d3e-4f5a-9b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c
```
